name: Adam Schmidt

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and was promoted from appliance showroom sales to junior manager of the installation-booking team at a large retail company. Five coordinators work with me, and I am still learning their budgets and the rules for assigning installers. I have a bachelor’s degree, but the experienced managers are quicker with the reports. I use the approved AI scheduler every day, then ring an installer before promising a customer that a cooker can be fitted on Friday.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner drives a delivery van on regular hours, and our grown children have places of their own. We still owe a little on our home and have four months of expenses saved. My pay is around the usual manager rate, and there are some other retail offices nearby. I like trying a new tool early, but I would not sell my family’s steady wages to chase a shiny job title. I have not checked what our retirement income would be.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the coordinators AI Plateau makes it easier to find an open slot, but the installer still has to say whether the right fitting kit is on the van. A customer needs the cooker working, not a beautifully timed appointment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think a small scheduling aid leaves my junior job mostly safe. We have four months saved, my partner has regular driving hours and the remaining home loan is manageable. I would keep learning the tool, but I would not make the household depend on its forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep my morning call with the installers about missing fittings. I would compare the AI slot list with ten completed appointments next week, then change a scheduling rule only after an installer confirms the cause of any failure. If the mild change arrives next year, I would keep that check and pay the loan as we normally do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job in this version. I would be embarrassed if the screen said complete while a family still had an unplugged cooker.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What failed appointment taught you that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last Friday the calendar showed a cooker fitted, but the installer had left because the wall socket was unsafe. The cooker customer still had no way to cook dinner after the installer left. I changed the status to unresolved and booked an electrical check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is using AI a new habit for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I already use the approved scheduler every day. I like finding what it gets wrong before we roll out another feature. Ten completed jobs are a small test I can verify myself.

say: An **open slot** is useful only when the fitter has the right kit.
I would report an **unfinished installation** as unresolved.
think: My **junior post** looks safe if AI only saves a little time.
Four months saved and **regular driving wages** steady our home loan.
do: **Keep** morning calls about missing installation fittings.
**Compare** AI slots with ten completed jobs; change a scheduling rule only after an installer confirms the failure’s cause.
feel: I feel **calm** but embarrassed by a falsely completed installation.
S0.quote: The cooker customer still had no way to cook dinner after the installer left.
fieldNote: His **daily AI use** is established; the ten-job comparison checks an existing scheduler.
His **four-month reserve** and two regular wages support calm in a mild case.

steps.text: Keep morning calls with installers about missing fitting kits
Compare ten completed jobs; change scheduling rule only after installer confirms failure cause

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say stronger AI may book installations and answer routine calls, so our five-person team could be reduced. I would show managers how many booked slots became working appliances, not just how fast the system filled a calendar. Installers should be paid for the time they spend correcting a bad booking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I might have to compete with another junior manager if offices are combined. I learn software quickly, but I am new to managing people and that matters when cuts come. Four months saved would give us breathing room, not a replacement wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the operations head for a paid three-week trial of an AI fault-flag tool, only with cover for the coordinators and installer time counted in the test. I would compare the flags with actual incomplete jobs and stop using it if it hides unsafe sockets. If our office shrinks, I would apply for posted service-desk manager jobs only with pay after travel that covers our loan and shifts fitting our shared schedule; I would accept only a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about being the newest manager in a smaller office. I also want to know whether a tool can spare an installer a pointless journey.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a useful flag?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A cooker appointment that needs an electrical check before a fitter goes out. We sent an installer to one home twice because the call notes had never mentioned the old socket. The second trip was wasted time for the worker and the family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a pay cut to keep using AI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. My partner’s van wage and our savings do not make a permanent lower salary harmless. I would check the offer and travel cost before leaving a paid post.

say: I would publish **working appliances**, not only filled slots, and account for installer time.
think: My **new manager seat** could face competition in an office merger.
Four months saved does not replace a **steady wage**.
do: **Request** a paid three-week fault-flag trial only with coordinator cover and counted installer time.
**Compare** AI flags with incomplete jobs and stop the trial if it hides unsafe sockets.
**Apply** for posted service jobs only with loan-covering net pay and workable shifts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about cuts and curious about fewer wasted journeys.
S1.quote: We sent an installer to one home twice because the call notes had never mentioned the old socket.
fieldNote: His **AI trial** needs paid time for installers and cover for the booking team.
A **new service job** requires a posting, net household pay, workable shifts and confirmed offer.

steps.text: Run paid three-week AI fault trial only with coordinator cover and counted installer time
Stop trial if fault flags hide unsafe sockets
Apply for posted service role only with loan-covering net pay and workable shifts
Accept only confirmed offer after checking travel cost and actual shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company AGI by 2028 could schedule installers and answer customers before it has told coordinators where they stand. I would ask for written notice and a rule for who can cancel an unsafe booking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect this booking office to lose most of its routine work, and my junior post may go. Another service desk also schedules and writes, so it faces 2028 AGI. Installing a cooker is physical until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I am not a qualified installer and cannot count on a training place or its wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask our staff committee for written severance and unsafe-booking authority. I would review our four-month reserve and home-loan dates with my partner. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I would apply for advertised local customer-service roles only if net pay after travel covers the loan and ordinary bills; I would accept only a real offer with hours we can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about the likely loss of booking work. Four months could buy a search, but it would not turn me into an electrician.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you become an installer straight away?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I can demonstrate a cooker in a showroom, but I have never signed off a wiring connection. I would need a qualified trainer and paid working hours. Installing a cooker does not begin with a job advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is an unsafe-booking rule?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A coordinator should be able to stop an appointment when the customer reports a damaged socket, even if the schedule is full. Sending a fitter to a known electrical hazard is not customer service. Someone with authority must change the slot.

say: **2028 AGI** could erase bookings before staff know their position.
I would seek written **unsafe-booking authority** and severance.
think: My **junior post** may go as routine booking work disappears.
Other service desks face **2028 AGI**; installation robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** staff committee this week for severance and unsafe-booking rules.
**Review** four-month reserve and loan dates with my partner.
**Apply** after a 2028 cut only to advertised roles with bill-covering net pay after travel and workable hours.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about likely booking cuts despite a four-month search window.
S2.quote: Installing a cooker does not begin with a job advert.
fieldNote: He rejects a **false installer fallback** because qualification, paid hours and actual places remain uncertain.
His **moderate reserve** allows a search but not a permanent reduction in household pay.

steps.text: Ask staff committee for written severance and authority to stop unsafe appointments
Apply after cut only to posted roles with bill-covering net pay after travel
Accept confirmed offer only after checking loan bills and workable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to test what a real installation apprenticeship requires and to pay people while they learn. I would ask the company to publish how many safe jobs its new schedule actually delivers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could consider learning the fitting side if it is a real paid route, but I do not yet have that skill. Booking reports face 2031 AGI, and physical installation meets capable robots around 2034. At 63 I would need to test whether I can handle the lifting and find out what retirement income is actually available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would request two paid mornings a month with an installer; I would attend only if the booking manager approves cover and a qualified fitter supervises without making me touch unsafe wiring. I would enter a fitting apprenticeship only if an actual place, funded fees, paid hours and a wage that keeps our loan current are offered. After 2031 I would take an advertised fitting-support job only with verified net pay and physical duties I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about starting again late, though five years allows a real test. A calendar lesson is easier than carrying a cooker up stairs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do on those mornings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Measure the doorway, check the fitting kit and watch the qualified installer identify when an electrician is needed. I would not wire a socket because I watched a video. The fitter would have to tell me what I got wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you spend savings on the apprenticeship?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We have four months saved and a loan to finish. I would use a funded place with paid hours, not ask my partner’s van wage to cover an unpaid training year.

say: A **five-year runway** should fund real installation learning with a qualified fitter on paid working time.
I would publish **safe completed jobs** alongside scheduling speed.
think: Booking reports face **2031 AGI**, with installation robots around 2034.
At **63**, lifting ability and retirement income are unverified.
do: **Request** paid installer mornings from 2027; attend only with booking cover and qualified supervision.
**Enter** fitting apprenticeship only with offered place, funded fees, paid hours and loan-sustaining wage.
**Take** post-2031 advertised fitting-support work only with viable net pay and manageable duties.
feel: I feel **anxious** about late training but able to test the work.
S3.quote: I would not wire a socket because I watched a video.
fieldNote: His **installer mornings** preserve booking cover and qualified supervision; he will not touch unsafe wiring.
An **apprenticeship** requires a real offer, funded fees, paid hours and enough wage for the home loan.

steps.text: Attend paid installer mornings only with booking cover and qualified fitter supervision
Enter offered fitting apprenticeship only with funded fees paid hours and loan-sustaining wage
Take advertised fitting-support job after 2031 only with viable net pay and manageable duties

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company a decade is enough to offer paid apprenticeships and set a clear safety rule for bookings. Customers should not be sent a fitter simply to make a booking system look busy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 by 2036 and might want to retire, but I have not checked any entitlement or amount. Booking and fitting-support paperwork face 2036 AGI, while physical installation meets robots around 2039. Four months saved gives room to choose, not a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep checking the fitting kit before appointments and ask for a retirement-income statement, comparing verified terms with our loan and bills. I would put sixty extra toward the loan only when both wages arrive in full, ordinary bills are paid and no vehicle repair bill is due. After 2036 I would stay in paid work while it is real if verified retirement income plus savings cannot cover our bills; I would stop only after we check the figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about what will pay the bills at 68. The longer lead time lets me lower debt, but it does not let me assume an income I have not seen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why pay extra on the loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It would reduce a fixed bill before I am 68, but I will not use our four-month savings to do it. The sixty would come only from a full-pay month. If my partner’s van needs repairs, the extra loan payment waits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make retirement real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A statement showing what income we actually qualify for, alongside our savings and the remaining loan. I will not ask our grown children to promise a monthly payment. They have their own homes to fund.

say: A **decade** should bring paid apprenticeships and safer booking rules.
I would reject **empty bookings** that send fitters to known hazards.
think: At **68**, retirement entitlement and amount are still unknown.
Booking reports face **2036 AGI**, while installation robots follow around 2039.
do: **Keep** checking fitting kits before appointments in 2026.
**Pay** sixty extra toward loan only after both full wages, ordinary bills and no vehicle repair cost.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 unless verified retirement income plus savings cover bills.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about unknown retirement income but able to reduce a fixed bill.
S4.quote: If my partner’s van needs repairs, the extra loan payment waits.
fieldNote: His **extra loan payment** uses new full-pay money, preserving four months of savings.
He will not infer **retirement entitlement** or support from grown children without actual figures.

steps.text: Keep checking fitting kits before cooker appointments
Pay sixty extra loan only with both full wages bills paid and no van repair cost
Continue paid work after 2036 unless verified retirement income plus savings cover bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. It could remove the booking desk before a paid installer place is open, and four months saved is not a new trade. Written severance, an unsafe-booking rule and a genuine paid training route would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the installer whether a booking became a working appliance. An appointment is not a hot meal. I would rather lose a tidy calendar score than send another family an unqualified promise.

headlineQuote: An appointment is not a hot meal.
portrait: **Adam, 58**, is a junior installation-booking manager, still learning budgets after showroom sales.
His **typical pay**, van-driver partner, four-month reserve and some nearby jobs support a remaining home loan.
He uses **AI daily** to schedule but checks fitting kits and unsafe sockets with installers.
He is **calm** under mild change, alarmed by fast booking cuts and cautious about an unfunded trade.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his junior desk before a real paid installation route exists.
whatWouldHelp: Written **severance**, unsafe-booking authority and a paid, qualified training place would help.
